# Git SSH auth

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-docs.mjs. Edit the manifest, then run `make docs`. -->

Configure git to clone private repositories over SSH with a deploy key

```yaml
- uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/actions/git-ssh-auth@v1
  with:
    ssh-private-key: # OpenSSH private key (a read-only deploy key). Pass it from a secret.
```

## How it works

Let git (and anything that shells out to it, like `terraform init`) clone private repos
over SSH, e.g. Terraform module sources written as `git::ssh://git@github.com/org/repo`.

No agent daemon: the key is written to $RUNNER_TEMP with 0600 permissions and git is
pointed at it through GIT_SSH_COMMAND for the rest of the job. $RUNNER_TEMP is wiped at
the end of every job on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, delete it yourself.

Host keys are never accepted on first use. By default GitHub's keys are fetched from
api.github.com/meta, over TLS, and pinned in a job-local known_hosts file.

Use a read-only deploy key scoped to the one repo it needs, not a personal key.

## Inputs

| Input | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ssh-private-key` | **yes** | — | OpenSSH private key (a read-only deploy key). Pass it from a secret. |
| `known-hosts` | no | `""` | known_hosts lines to trust. Empty fetches github.com's published host keys from api.github.com/meta, which is what you want for GitHub-hosted repos. |

## Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `key-path` | Path of the private key file written for this job. |
